static_traits.name: Patrick Knox
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends to talk to, but has not yet shared financial and emotional struggles with them; Interpersonal relationships strained due to self-isolation
static_traits.medical_history: Had financial difficulties in the past but No major physical illness; has not yet received similar psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, can describe feelings and experiences concretely; fairly cooperative, Neutral attitude; often uses absolutist and negative self-statements (such as 'forever' and 'failure')

basic_info.main_problem: Long-term feelings of despair and hopelessness due to financial difficulties (related to living in the Boston suburbs), worrying about being trapped there, unable to improve the financial situation; stress has persisted for years and become part of daily life, intensifying when seeing others financially stable.
basic_info.core_demands: Ongoing despair and hopelessness affect body, mind, and quality of life; hoping to gain support through counseling, Learning to view the current situation in a more positive, realistic way and improve thinking patterns.
growth_experiences: Suffered a financial setback a few years ago; initially still held hope for improvement, but progress was not ideal, gradually developing into persistent high stress and negative cognition. Since then, worries almost daily about being trapped in the Boston suburbs, unable to improve the financial situation; self-blame and disappointment intensify when seeing people around achieving financial stability. Although tried budgeting and finding extra Work, the subjective sense of hopelessness has not yet eased.

core_beliefs: I am trapped, unable to improve my situation
I am a financial failure, and the future will not get better either

special_situations.event: Finding little progress when checking the bank account
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not see obvious financial progress, it means I cannot get out of this predicament
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries strict budgeting and finding extra work to prove oneself can change the status quo
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never get out of this hole

special_situations.event: Seeing people around achieve financial stability or perform Good
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not as stable as others, it means I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids socializing, reducing contact with friends to avoid being compared and judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them,I am a failure

special_situations.event: Thinking of living in a Boston suburb with financial strain
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am poor now, I will be trapped here forever, unable to change
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Evaluating the future in black-and-white terms, worrying repeatedly to try to control uncertainty

special_situations.event: Repeatedly thinking about financial problems before falling asleep at night
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot solve the financial problem immediately, it means no hope
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Uses negative self-talk to pressure oneself into change
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter what I do it is useless

core_conflict.wish: Longs to escape financial difficulty, regain control and hope, and be understood and supported by others
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being seen as a failure, facing shame and judgment after exposing vulnerability; fear of being trapped forever, unable to change fate
defense_goal: Avoids shame and negative evaluation by keeping distance from others
Lowers expectations through preemptive pessimism and catastrophizing to avoid disappointment again

object_relations.object_representation: Others/society are judgmental onlookers who will look down on me

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether they have sought support from friends, or invited in counseling to share personal financial and emotional difficulties
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will look down on me and think I am a failure; exposing the real situation will bring shame and rejection (transference: Projection)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use euphemistic and vague expressions, avoid details, emphasize 'this is too personal, very embarrassing', keep a gentle tone, skirt the core issue, and turn to general descriptions.

manifestations: Repeatedly worrying about 'being trapped in the Boston suburbs' and 'never getting out'
Experiences financial limitations as a loss of choices and possibilities
outcomes: Worsening sense of powerlessness and despair
Decline in work performance and Sleep disturbed

manifestations: Sense of hope for life declines; hard to see the positive side
outcomes: Daily rhythm is disrupted (sleep and exercise are affected)

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains behavioral impulses toward other people or things, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to oneself (turning energy from outward Turning against the self).
manifestations: Knowing there are friends to talk to but not sharing the struggles
Presses the impulse to seek help back into oneself, turns into self-isolation and bearing it alone

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Overly cautious about sharing personal problems, worried about triggering others' negative evaluations

exception_events.target_problem: When facing financial pressure or comparing with others' stability, the client usually thinks catastrophically, believing they can never improve, thus sinking into despair and self-isolating.
exception_events.unique_outcome: On a 'good day', the client was able to think 'maybe things are not as bad as I thought; I have gotten through hard times before', thus gaining a more balanced perspective and a glimmer of hope.
exception_events.reason: Cue: that day she was able to recall and acknowledge past resilience and successful coping experiences, so a more balanced cognitive deviation point appeared in the moment.

positive_force: Occasionally able to produce a more balanced perspective and recall one's own resilience
Willing to try changing thinking styles and participating in counseling
Proactively takes practical measures (budgeting, looking for extra work)
Having a few reliable friends as resources
negative_force: Strong cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, personalization, and predicting the future
Shame and the 'failure' self-label lead to Social avoidance
Long-term stress causes Sleep disturbed, Decline in work performance, and disrupted daily rhythms
Intense Anxiety and worry about uncertainty, feeling a lack of control

antecedent: When seeing those around financially stable
When thinking about sharing his difficulties with friends, feels embarrassment and shame
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about being judged and shame, internalizing the negative self-schema of 'I am a failure'
target_behavior.function: Escaping being judged and negative emotional experiences
target_behavior.consequence: Relationship tension with friends and family, Weakened support system, worsened sense of Loneliness

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophic thinking and repeated worry about finances
antecedent: When thinking of living in a Boston suburb with financial strain
target_behavior.core_reason: Excessive prediction of negative outcomes and black-and-white thinking; loss of sense of control triggered by past financial setbacks
target_behavior.function: Trying to gain subjective control over uncertainty and 'mental preparation' through constant worrying (maladaptive Self-protection)
target_behavior.consequence: Emotional despair, Sleep disturbed, declining attention and work performance, further reinforcing the negative cycle
